detailed_rationale:
ACME Solar Holdings is one of India's larger renewable independent power producers, running an integrated solar, wind, hybrid and 'firm dispatchable renewable energy' (FDRE) portfolio across ten states under long-term (typically 25-year) power purchase agreements. Growth has been strong on the back of new capacity commissioning: TTM sales growth of 48% and a 5-year profit CAGR of 51%, with Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) revenue of Rs 858 crore at an 86% operating margin -- a very high margin typical of annuity-like PPA-backed generation once a plant is commissioned.

The returns on that growth are underwhelming relative to the price being paid for it: ROE of just 10.4% and ROCE of 8.89%, against Rs 19,896 crore of borrowings versus only Rs 4,940 crore of equity reserves -- a heavily leveraged capacity-addition model, with a further Rs 4,358 crore of capital work-in-progress signalling more debt-funded build-out ahead. The stock trades at 44.1x earnings and 4.41x book, rich multiples for a regulated-PPA-return business generating low-teens ROE, and promoter holding fell a full 11.9 percentage points in the latest quarter alone -- a sizeable stake reduction that, combined with a recent Rs 2,800 crore QIP, suggests both fresh dilution and promoter monetisation happening at the same time as the stock trades near its richest multiples.

Reverse-DCF: 44x earnings and 4.4x book for a business earning under 9% ROCE only works if capacity additions continue at a rapid, uninterrupted pace for many years and financing costs stay benign -- a lot to ask of a heavily levered capex story where the promoter itself has just meaningfully reduced its stake. I judge the multiple rich relative to the return profile actually being delivered, and side with the quant Sell.
recommendation_rationale: Revenue and capacity growth are genuinely strong, but ROE/ROCE (10.4%/8.9%) are modest for a 44x P/E, leverage is heavy (nearly Rs 20,000 crore of debt against under Rs 5,000 crore of equity reserves), and the promoter cut its stake by almost 12 percentage points in the latest quarter even as fresh QIP capital came in. That combination of rich valuation, thin returns and reduced promoter conviction keeps this at Sell.
summary: ACME Solar is a fast-growing renewable power producer with long-term contracted revenue, but its returns on capital (under 9% ROCE) are modest for a stock trading at over 44 times earnings and more than 4 times book value, and the business carries close to Rs 20,000 crore of debt to fund its expansion. The promoter also reduced its stake by nearly 12 percentage points in the most recent quarter. We rate this a Sell given the valuation is ahead of what the returns currently justify.
positive_para: ACME Solar has genuine scale and growth in a structurally growing sector (renewable capacity addition in India), with 48% TTM revenue growth, very high 86% operating margins typical of contracted PPA generation, and revenue visibility from 25-year power purchase agreements that reduce demand-side uncertainty once plants are commissioned.
negative_para: Returns on capital are modest (10.4% ROE, 8.9% ROCE) for a stock priced at 44x earnings and 4.4x book, and the business is heavily levered (~Rs 19,900 crore of debt versus ~Rs 4,900 crore of equity reserves) to fund continued capacity growth, with a large capital-work-in-progress balance signalling more debt ahead. The promoter's stake fell almost 12 percentage points in a single quarter even as the company raised fresh QIP capital, a combination worth watching closely for existing holders.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 44x P/E and 4.4x book value for a business earning under 9% ROCE requires years of uninterrupted, rapid, debt-funded capacity growth at benign financing costs to be justified. Given the leverage already on the balance sheet and the promoter's own large stake reduction this quarter, I judge the current multiple rich relative to the return profile actually being delivered.
